summary: Quarter-start all-hands focused on velocity targets, org structure adjustments, and product go-to-market priorities. Leadership reviewed performance signals, highlighted risk areas around Dedicated capacity SLAs, and surfaced a small restructuring to reduce handoffs between infra and runtime teams. Open Q&A about compensation pacing and hiring plan. Technical snippet: kernel selection dashboard will be shared; plan to run dedicated burst pilot with two customers in Feb.

Product prioritization for Optimize and Console
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-12 10:00 PST (78 min) - Winter Velocity & Structure Checkpoint
Attendees: Aisha (CEO), Liam (CTO), Marta (VP Prod), Devon (Head Eng), Grace (People), plus remote squads.

00:00 Speaker: Aisha Khan - Good morning everyone, uh welcome to the winter velocity and structure checkpoint. Happy new year, um we're, we're starting at 10 on the dot, thanks for being punctual. Quick agenda: product priorities, a small structure change, and then an open q and a. We'll try to keep this to an hour but I think we have about 75, 80 minutes.

00:30 Speaker: Liam O'Connor - Hey all, real quick on infra signals: late December we saw a 12% tail latency jump on long-context generative traces, the KV cache hit-rate dipped during sustained bursts, so we've prioritized kernel selection and batching tweaks. I'll share the dashboard link after this call, it's in the thread. Some of the transcribed names in the chart might read K V cash in the export, ignore that.

01:05 Speaker: Marta Reyes - From product: Optimize beta is shipping next week to internal teams, then to a handful of partners. We're focusing on two levers: smarter prefix caching and quantization recommendations per workload. We'll be collecting perf and quality signals, and we've built a prompt-set driven eval so we can watch regressions.

01:40 Speaker: Devon Patel - Engineering note: to reduce handoffs the runtime and infra squads will align under a new "Serving Platform" tribe — this is a small reorg, not a headcount cut. Goal is faster ownership for end-to-end latency and rollout policies. We'll keep the Dedicated ops and customer-facing infra intact. Details will be on the doc — link in the followup.

02:15 Speaker: Grace Lin - On people: we'll open a feedback window, and there's a town hall in two weeks to collect questions. Compensation review timeline remains Q2; we'll try to speed up promotions for critical roles. If you have questions about relocation or role changes, please use the private channel.

03:00 Speaker: Attendee (S1) - Quick question: um how will this affect the SE runway for customers who need VPC/on-prem support?

03:15 Speaker: Devon Patel - Good question. Short answer: minimal impact to customer support. The on-prem/VPC cohort stays under the Private deployments org, but insite infra and runtime will partner more closely during rollouts so it should reduce coordination lag.

03:50 Speaker: Attendee (S2) - Will there be any change to Dedicated SLA commitments? A lot of clients asked after the december incident.

04:10 Speaker: Liam O'Connor - We're proposing a burst pilot with two anchor customers in February to validate autoscale playbooks and fallback model routing. SLAs are not being loosened; rather we're adding layered fallback and faster rollback. We'll also add more traceable audit logs to make root cause faster to identify.

04:45 Speaker: Aisha Khan - I want to call out priorities: top priority is reliability (SLA/latency), second is product outcomes for customers, third is cost efficiency. We will not chase cost at the expense of predictable latency for enterprise customers.

05:20 Speaker: Marta Reyes - On product tradeoffs: some teams want aggressive quantization for cost, others worry about hallucination regressions. Our approach will be: model/quantization recommendations per workload with guardrails in the Optimize UI — we'll present a canary policy for internal usage first.

06:00 Speaker: Attendee (S3) - Can you clarify what the "Serving Platform" tribe ownership looks like day to day? Like who owns canary rollbacks?

06:18 Speaker: Devon Patel - Owning end-to-end means runtime owns canary rollouts and rollback automation for model variants; infra still owns physical capacity and cluster autoscaler, but they share SLO dashboards and a single incident oncall. Practically this reduces the ping-pong during incidents.

06:55 Speaker: Attendee (S4) - Regarding hiring: will we continue to hire across the board or focus on infra/runtime?

07:10 Speaker: Grace Lin - Hiring plan: we will prioritize infra/runtime, customer reliability, and then product ops. We have budget to hire ~18 FTEs this quarter, distributed across Palo Alto, Dublin, and a small remote budget for specialized hires.

07:45 Speaker: Attendee (S5) - On shared artifacts: someone mentioned a perf benchmarking sheet and the kernel selection dashboard — can we get links?

08:00 Speaker: Liam O'Connor - Yes, I'll post the kernel selection perf dashboard (note: the sheet has a couple of mis-typed model names in the export — check model ids, not display names). Link will be in #infra-updates.

08:30 Speaker: Aisha Khan - Ok next section is open Q&A, please drop questions in the thread or raise hands.

09:10 Speaker: Attendee (S6) - Is the restructuring permanent or will we revisit in 6 months?

09:25 Speaker: Aisha Khan - We'll run a feedback loop and review outcomes at the end of Q1; if the change isn't improving cycle time and reliability we'll iterate. This is meant to be an experiment with clear metrics.

10:00 Speaker: Attendee (S7) - Any update on partner go-to-market? Are we reprioritizing channel partnerships?

10:18 Speaker: Marta Reyes - We will prioritize a smaller set of partner integrations for this quarter — ones that help with enterprise adoption and compliance. We're deferring some experimental marketplace pushes to Q3.

10:40 Speaker: Attendee (S8) - Regarding compliance: are we getting any new requests for stricter data residency or audit controls?

11:00 Speaker: Liam O'Connor - Yes, a few enterprise prospects asked for region-specific audit logs and tighter KMS integrations. We're fast-tracking a KMS/HSM checklist for Private installs and adding region tags to audit traces. Some of the verbiage may be garbled in this transcript (S O C two spelled as sock two), but we'll attach the compliance FAQ in the followup.

11:40 Speaker: Attendee (S9) - If we need to pause a rollout mid-canary, who's empowered to do that?

11:55 Speaker: Devon Patel - Oncall for Serving Platform and the product PM for that rollout have joint authority to pause; engineering lead will execute the rollback. This is to ensure speed and proper communication.

12:30 Speaker: Aisha Khan - Quick leadership note: I've asked comms to draft a message to customers explaining the org adjustment and reassurance on SLAs; we'll share before end of week. Also, please treat the feedback thread as anonymous if you want — People Ops will collate.

13:05 Speaker: Attendee (S10) - Two personal asks: 1) could we get clearer docs on the Optimize beta for internal use, and 2) can we have a daily short sync for infra incidents until the canary automation is stable?

13:30 Speaker: Marta Reyes - Yes to both. We'll publish a short internal FAQ and run a temporary daily incident stand for the next three weeks.

14:00 Speaker: Closing - Aisha Khan - Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and the reorg doc. Action items will be posted. Keep feedback coming.

End of transcript.

Referenced artifacts: "kernel-selection-dashboard" (link posted in #infra-updates), Optimize beta draft (doc link), compliance FAQ (to be attached). Some transcription artifacts: "K V cash" should read "KV cache", "sock two" is SOC 2, and occasional speaker labels are simplified (Attendee S1 etc.).
